newsitem.title: USA: Varlen Corp ties net income drop to interest costs.
newsitem.headline: Varlen Corp ties net income drop to interest costs.

text.p: Varlen Corp said on Monday that higher interest expenses from its purchase of the Brenco railcar bearing unit cut third quarter net income but that the new arm and its core businesses helped it post record sales and operating profits for the period.

"Though net income did decline in the third quarter, we're seeing once again that the strength of our core businesses can help us to endure the periods of weaker demand in certain of our served markets," said Richard Wellek, president and chief executive officer in an earnings statement.
It said net income in the third quarter fell to $0.53 per share fully diluted on sales of $119.9 million from $0.64 per share in the year-ago period on sales of $94.2 million.
The automotive products business kept its momentum, with record results in the quarter despite work disruptions at General Motors Corp in Canada and the United States, the company said.
Wellek called the Brenco purchase "a major strategic step forward," with Brenco's big U.S. marketshare positioning Varlen to "take advantage of opportunities in international markets."
Varlen makes railroad, heavy-duty truck/trailer and automotive transportation products. Its shares traded up 3/8 at 19-1/8.
